issue.title: Support DagBundle based deployment for Coordinator

labels.name: area:coordinator
labels.description: Coordinator: The interface to spawn Lang-SDK subprocesses

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
- closes: https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/66334

## Why

Language-SDK subprocess coordinators (Java, Executable, Node) required a hand-managed filesystem root (`jars_root` / `executables_root` / `bundles_root`) for compiled artifacts. Users should be able to deploy those artifacts by existing DagBundle mechanism as well.

## How

- Add an optional `dag_bundle_name` kwarg on the `SubprocessCoordinator` base, giving three ways to locate artifacts:
  - explicit root set: scan that path (unchanged legacy behavior).
  - `dag_bundle_name` set: scan that configured bundle's path.
  - neither set: scan the task's own bundle, co-located with the Python stub Dag.
- Resolve roots in the base and expose them through `_get_scan_roots()` while keeping the existing `_build_execute_task_command(what)` hook signature, so a subclass only declares its explicit-root kwarg through `_explicit_artifact_roots`.
- Materialize the bundle through `airflow.sdk.execution_time.bundles.initialize_ti_bundle`, a new module split out of `task_runner` so starting a language-SDK task does not import the task runner into the supervisor.
- Validate at construction that an explicit root and `dag_bundle_name` are not both set, and that a named bundle is configured, via a new `DagBundlesManager.is_bundle_configured` that reads configured names without importing any bundle class.

## Notes

- Version semantics: a co-located bundle is pinned to the run's `bundle_info.version` because it is the same artifact the run was created from; a separately named artifact bundle resolves to the version current when the task starts. Either way the bundle is materialized at a concrete version, so `BundleVersionLock` protects the same tree the subprocess scans.

issue.title: Parse native Java Dags and show their source

labels.name: area:coordinator
labels.description: Coordinator: The interface to spawn Lang-SDK subprocesses

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
Stack (bottom to top): #73841, #74004, #73842, **#73843**, #73844, #73845, #73846, #73847

- related: #71929
- Part of the native Dag e2e stack. Builds on the native Dag parse layer ([new commits only](https://github.com/apache/airflow/compare/jason/lang-sdk-e2e/03-native-dag-parse...jason/lang-sdk-e2e/04-java-dag-importer)).
- Merge after #71190, which makes the Java runtime answer the Dag-parsing request.

## Why

With this PR, `JavaCoordinator` parses the native Dags a bundle JAR declares, and the Code view shows their Java source.

## What changes

- **Which JARs.** A `JavaCoordinator` without `jars_root` parses each `.jar` whose manifest sets `Main-Class` (matching `main_class` if set) in the Dag bundles it reads, skipping thin-bundle dependency JARs. An unreadable JAR is kept so its parse reports the error.
- **Parse command.** The task command, `java -classpath <bundle JARs> <jvm_args> <Main-Class>`, with the same schema version lookup. A JAR it cannot run gets an import error.
- **Manifest reader.** Tasks and parses now read manifests per the JAR specification (CR, LF or CRLF, folded lines, main section only). The old `email` parser broke a folded `Main-Class`.
- **Dag source.** The Gradle plugin packs the main class's `.java` file, or `airflowBundle.dagSource`, into every bundle JAR, fat or thin, and names it in the manifest. `get_source_code` returns it, up to 1 MiB, or a placeholder. A JAR embeds one source for all its Dags, so the Java importer ignores the Dag id.

The Java runtime is unchanged here. The Java SDK layer above makes it answer the parse request, with a payload that passes `validate_serialized_dag`.

```ini
[sdk]
coordinators = {
  "java-native": {
    "classpath": "airflow.sdk.coordinators.java.JavaCoordinator",
    "kwargs": {"java_executable": "/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk/bin/java"}
  }
}
queue_to_coordinator = {"java-native": "java-native"}
```

```groovy
airflowBundle {
    mainClass = "com.example.Main"
    dagSource = file("src/main/java/com/example/MyDag.java")  // optional
}
```

Example bundle manifest (`./gradlew bundle` in `java-sdk/example`):

```text
Manifest-Version: 1.0
Airflow-Java-SDK-Dag-Code: META-INF/airflow/dag-code/org/apache/airflow/
 example/ExampleBundleBuilder.java
Airflow-Supervisor-Schema-Version: 2026-10-30
Main-Class: org.apache.airflow.example.ExampleBundleBuilder
Multi-Release: true
```

## Deviations and limitations

- #71929 leaves `get_source_code` open for native Dags. This returns the source embedded as the pure Java Dags ADR (#70156) proposes, but under `META-INF/airflow/dag-code/` instead of the JAR root to avoid fat JAR collisions, and without its `airflow-metadata.yaml`, since the parse runs the JVM.
- With several executable JARs in a bundle and no `main_class`, each is parsed, but a task runs the first one in walk order (#71134).
- The Java SDK (#71190) still writes the stock values of `max_active_tasks`, `max_active_runs`, `max_consecutive_failed_dag_runs`, `catchup` and `disable_bundle_versioning` when a Dag leaves them unset, so a native Java Dag does not get the Airflow config values that #73842 fills in.
- Documented: tasks need `queue` set, no Dag in both Java and Python in one bundle, no cluster policies, `airflow dags reserialize` does not store a JAR's Dags, and `airflow dags test`, `tasks test`, `tasks render` and `tasks list` refuse a native Java Dag.

## Verification

- `task-sdk/tests/task_sdk/coordinators/java`: 88 passed. Java SDK `./gradlew test` at this layer passed.
- The Maven snippet added to the docs was not built.

issue.title: Java SDK: answer TaskHandlerParseRequest with registered handlers

labels.name: area:coordinator
labels.description: Coordinator: The interface to spawn Lang-SDK subprocesses

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
Stack (bottom to top), on native #74037 (stack #74170): #73973, #73974, #73975, **#73977**, #73976, #74067, #74135, #74140, #74141, #73971, #74030, #74031, #74032, #74136, #74137, #74138, #74139

## Why

The Dag processor will check each stub task against the task handler that the artifact a worker would run registers ([ADR-0011](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/airflow-core/adr/lang-sdk/0011-mixed-language-dag-processing.md), [ADR-0012](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/airflow-core/adr/lang-sdk/0012-lang-sdk-parse-protocol.md)). #73974 added the probe and the coordinator hooks, and #73975 made Go bundles answer. Today a Java bundle fails on a `TaskHandlerParseRequest` as an unexpected first frame.

This PR makes a Java bundle answer with every handler registered through `@Builder.TaskHandler` or `Bundle.register(dagId, taskId, cls)` and how each handler's parameters bind. It also lets `JavaCoordinator` find the JAR a stub task would run and start it for the probe. Nothing calls the probe yet: #74135 does.

## What changes

A Java bundle registers task handlers as before:

```java
public static class ReportInput implements TaskInput {
  @ArgName("run_label") public String label;
  public long transformed;
}

@Builder.TaskHandler(dag = "etl", task = "transform")
public long transform(Client client, long extracted, List<Double> weights) { ... }

@Builder.TaskHandler(dag = "etl", task = "report")
public void report(ReportInput input) { ... }
```

When the Dag processor probes it, the bundle replies with every task handler it registers, keyed by Dag id. `task_handlers` depends only on the JAR, never on the request, and `fileloc` repeats the request's `file`.

```python
TaskHandlerParsingResult(
    fileloc="/bundles/java/etl.jar",
    task_handlers={"etl": [
        TaskHandlerDeclaration(task_id="transform", binding="positional", params=[
            TaskHandlerParam(name="extracted", value_schema={"type": "integer", "format": "int64"}),
            TaskHandlerParam(name="weights", value_schema={"anyOf": [
                {"type": "array", "items": {"anyOf": [{"type": "number", "format": "double"}, {"type": "null"}]}},
                {"type": "null"}]}),
        ]),
        TaskHandlerDeclaration(task_id="report", binding="named", params=[
            TaskHandlerParam(name="run_label", exact_name=True,
                             value_schema={"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}]}),
            TaskHandlerParam(name="transformed", value_schema={"type": "integer", "format": "int64"}),
        ]),
    ]},
)
```

### Java runtime

- **Task handlers only.** Only `@Builder.TaskHandler` classes and `Bundle.register(dagId, taskId, cls)` are declared, in registration order, and no handler runs. The tasks of a Dag declared in Java (`DagDef`, `@Builder.Dag`) are never task handlers, so the reply leaves them out. A test pins this, and the `Server` KDoc says so.
- **Dag tasks are refused.** The processor marks each class it generates for a `@Builder.Dag` task with `@GeneratedDagTask`, and `Bundle.register(dagId, taskId, cls)` rejects such a class. Its task belongs to a Dag declared in Java, so the error tells the author to declare a task handler with `@Builder.TaskHandler`. A test fails without the check, and the `Bundle.register` KDoc and `java-sdk/README.md` say so.
- **Binding.** Flat data parameters are `positional`, with their Java names. A `TaskInput` (as the only data parameter, or as an `InputTask<I>`) is `named`, and `@ArgName` fields match exactly. A handler that reads no argument is `named` with no params, so the Dag processor only warns about an argument passed to it.
- **Parameter names.** Java drops parameter names at compile time unless built with `-parameters`. So the annotation processor gives each class it generates for a `@Builder.TaskHandler` method a static `AIRFLOW_TASK_PARAMS` field with its flat parameters' names and declared types, or its `TaskInput` type. `@Builder.Dag` task classes get no such field.
- **`value_schema`** is the declared Java type in the vocabulary `build_arg_bindings` emits for a Python annotation:
  - only primitives exclude null;
  - arrays, collections and maps describe their items, and a POJO is `{"type": "object"}` without its fields;
  - `String`, the boxed numbers, `BigInteger`, `BigDecimal`, `UUID`, `Duration` and the `java.time` date and time types (`OffsetDateTime`, `ZonedDateTime`, `LocalDateTime`, `Instant`, `LocalDate`, `LocalTime`) each get a schema;
  - `byte[]`, `Object`, `Optional`, `Date`, `URI` and the `java.time` types not listed above (such as `OffsetTime` and `Period`) get none;
  - an enum lists its constant names, sorted, because `Class.getFields` has no defined order;
  - it does not widen for the decoder's coercions (it also turns `"5"` into a `long`), as pydantic's schemas do for its lax mode.
- **Reply shape.** The generated models cannot hold `task_handlers`, so the reply is a plain map. An SDK test checks its keys, required fields and binding values against the vendored supervisor schema.
- **Reply handshake.** The runtime waits for the parent's acknowledgement before it exits, so the parent has the result first.

### Vendored supervisor schema

`java-sdk/sdk/schema/schema.json` was refreshed only when its `api_version` changed, by downloading the published file. A version is published only at release, so the in-progress `2026-10-30` returns 404 and messages added during the cycle never reached the Java models.

- The Gradle task `:sdk:syncSupervisorSchema` now copies the Task SDK snapshot when it declares the configured version. It downloads the published file as before otherwise.
- Code generation reads only the committed `schema.json`, and the snapshot is copied only with `java-sdk/gradlew -p java-sdk :sdk:syncSupervisorSchema`, then commit the file. No build step runs the task, so a later change to the Task SDK snapshot neither rewrites the file nor fails `ktlint`. A read-only `:sdk:checkSupervisorSchemaVersion` fails generation when the file is not at the configured version.
- The refresh brings in the task handler messages, and main's changes since the last vendoring (`DagSourceCode`, `UpdateDagRunNote`, `retry_reason`, `multi_team` and more required fields). It also drops `map_index` and `element_index` from `XComArgBinding`, which the Task SDK snapshot never declared; `ArgBinding.kt` still reads them from the raw map, so decoding does not change. The Java SDK and its tests need no other change.
- The `sync-java-sdk-supervisor-schema` hook stays a version-only check at the pre-commit stage and runs the task only when the configured version changes. Only the hook's docstring and prek description changed.

### Coordinator

- `JavaCoordinator._find_task_handler_artifact(bundle_path=..., dag_id=...)` is the worker's own scan (`_JarInfo.find`, `main_class` included), so the Dag processor checks the JAR a worker would run. The Dag id plays no part, because a task of any Dag runs the same Main-Class.
- It returns the resolved path of the JAR that sets that Main-Class. The scan can stop on another JAR, such as the `airflow-sdk` JAR that gives a thin JAR its schema version, so `_JarInfo` now records the path. A caller computes the path in the Dag bundle relative to `bundle_path.resolve()`.
- `JavaCoordinator._build_parse_task_handler_command(path=...)` is a task's own command, so the probe answers for the classpath and Main-Class a worker would run. Without `main_class` that is the scan's pick (#71134).
- #73974's gate applies: the probe starts only a runtime whose schema version is at least `2026-10-30`, and the Java SDK reports it.
- A JAR built from main's Java SDK before this change also reports `2026-10-30` but cannot answer, so its probe fails. #74135 then logs a warning, and rebuilding the bundle fixes it.

### Bundles

The example, the e2e test bundle, the Scala Spark example and the k8s example registered the Java tasks of Python-owned Dags as a Dag declared in Java, which the reply never reports. They now register those tasks as task handlers. Execution already falls back to task handlers, so runs do not change.

### Docs

- The contributor guide (`30_new_language_sdk.rst`) says `JavaCoordinator` implements both hooks.
- `java-sdk/README.md` describes the parse and the rejection of a `@Builder.Dag` task class. A task of a Python Dag is a `@Builder.TaskHandler` or a hand-written `Task` class registered with `Bundle.register(dagId, taskId, cls)`.

Builds on #73974 (hooks, `parse_task_handler`, the gate, the probe) and #73973 (the models), and on native #74036 (`_build_command`, `_JarInfo` with its sorted walk, `read_main_attributes`). No user docs: #74135 adds them.

## How to test

```bash
java-sdk/gradlew -p java-sdk build
uv run --project scripts pytest scripts/tests/ci/prek/test_sync_java_sdk_supervisor_schema.py -q
uv run --project task-sdk --with-editable shared/secrets_masker pytest task-sdk/tests/task_sdk/coordinators -q
uv run --project airflow-core --with-editable shared/secrets_masker pytest airflow-core/tests/unit/dag_processing/ -q
# Builds java-sdk/example as a thin bundle and probes it:
AIRFLOW_LANG_SDK_REAL_PROBE_TESTS=1 uv run --project airflow-core --with-editable shared/secrets_masker pytest airflow-core/tests/unit/dag_processing/test_task_handler_processor_java.py -q
SKIP=lychee-docker,regenerate-java-sdk-verification-metadata prek run --from-ref <parent> --to-ref HEAD --stage pre-commit
prek run mypy-task-sdk --all-files
prek run mypy-airflow-core --all-files
```

Ran:

- Java SDK, JDK 11 (Temurin 11.0.32.1): `java-sdk/gradlew -p java-sdk build --rerun-tasks` passed with 202 tests against 190 before (processor 24, sdk 150, jpl 10, jul 6, log4j2 5, slf4j 7). `:sdk:checkSupervisorSchemaVersion` passes (`api_version=2026-10-30`), the build leaves `schema.json` untouched, and `cmp` shows it identical to the monorepo snapshot.
- scripts: the sync hook tests, 5 passed. Main had none.
- Scratch repo with the `ktlint`, `spotless` and sync hooks, `java-sdk` and both schemas, after adding a `$defs` entry to the snapshot at the same `api_version`: `prek run ktlint --all-files` failed with `files were modified` before this change, because the build copied the snapshot over `schema.json`. Now all three hooks pass with `--all-files`, a Gradle build leaves the file untouched, and `java-sdk/gradlew -p java-sdk :sdk:syncSupervisorSchema` copies the snapshot when asked. When the configured version and the snapshot move together, a build fails on the check and names that command, and the sync hook refreshes the file.
- task-sdk `coordinators/`: 412 passed, run serially. `java/test_coordinator.py` goes from 57 to 74 tests: `TestMainJar` (3 new, 5 updated), `TestFindTaskHandlerArtifact` (8) and `TestBuildParseTaskHandlerCommand` (6, including the probe exec).
- airflow-core `dag_processing/`: 747 passed, 10 skipped (the 8 that need a backend, the FAB auth manager or the system test Dags, and the two real probes without their variable).
- The real Java probe with `AIRFLOW_LANG_SDK_REAL_PROBE_TESTS=1`: 1 passed in 18 s with a warm Gradle cache, on JDK 11. It finds `probe-example.jar` (the `airflow-sdk` JAR beside it sets the schema version) and the probe answers with the three Dags that register task handlers. The native `java_native_interface_example` Dag is left out.
- The four fixtures build against the working-tree SDK through an included build, so nothing is published. The e2e and k8s bundles build on JDK 11 (25 JARs each). The Scala Spark example builds a thin bundle of 167 JARs on JDK 17. Without `main_class` the scan stops on `javassist.CtClass`, because five dependency JARs set a Main-Class, so such a bundle needs `main_class`. With it set, the find returns `compile-scala.jar` and the probe answers `scala_spark_example` with `spark_extract`, `spark_transform` and `spark_load`, each `named` with no params.
- Each commit passes its own tests when checked out alone.
- Each new test fails without its change:
  - The sync hook's logic is unchanged, so its tests pin the existing version-only check and also pass against the base script. The check task and the on-request copy have no unit test, and the scratch-repo run above covers them.
  - Restoring the old `BuilderProcessor.kt` fails 11 processor tests: three for the handler params field and eight for the marker. Dropping only the marker fails the eight.
  - Removing the check from `Bundle.register` fails `shouldRejectClassGeneratedForDagTask`.
  - `ValueSchemaTest` does not compile without `ValueSchema.kt`, and dropping `.sorted()` fails the scalar test.
  - Restoring the old `Server.kt` fails both Server parse tests, the second on its check of the error (`Unexpected initial frame` instead of `Coordinator comm closed`), not on a timeout. Adding the Dags of the bundle to the reply fails two `TaskHandlerParseTest` tests and the Server answer test. Renaming `exact_name` fails the schema check, and swallowing the missing acknowledgement fails `failsTaskHandlerParseWithoutAcknowledgement`.
  - 22 of the new or updated coordinator tests fail on the old coordinator. Recording the path on the schema-version branch instead of the Main-Class branch fails three, an unresolved path fails the symlink test, building the probe command with `_build_jar_command` fails the two-JARs test, and scanning the directory of the found JAR instead of the scan roots fails the `app/` and `libs/` layout test.
  - With the old `Server.kt` the real probe returns no handlers and `The Lang-SDK runtime exited with code 1 without a parse result`. With the old coordinator the find raises `NotImplementedError`, and with the old example `java_interface_example` is missing.
- `prek` over the whole range at the pre-commit stage passed with `lychee-docker` and `regenerate-java-sdk-verification-metadata` skipped (66 hooks passed, the rest had no files to check, including `check-supervisor-schemas-versions`). The Task SDK schema, `airflow-core/src`, the Go and TS SDKs and the Gradle plugin are untouched. `mypy-task-sdk`, `mypy-airflow-core`, `mypy-scripts` and the sync hook pass with `--all-files`.

issue.title: Run exactly the artifact a stub task is bound to

labels.name: area:coordinator
labels.description: Coordinator: The interface to spawn Lang-SDK subprocesses

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
Stack (bottom to top): #73970, #73971, #73972, #73973, #73974, #73975, #73976, #73977, #74030, #74031, #74032, #74033, #74067, #74135, #74136, #74137, **#74138**, #74139, #74140, #74141

## Why

The scheduler now sends a stub task the artifact the Dag processor bound it to, but the worker still searches a bundle for an artifact that declares the task's Dag id, so it can run another artifact than the bound one. This PR has the worker run exactly the file it is pointed at ([ADR-0013](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/airflow-core/adr/lang-sdk/0013-persisted-task-handler-bindings.md) "Flow 3"), deletes the search, and fails a task whose artifact cannot be resolved in the task runtime with the reason in its task log. It also removes the known limit of the previous PR: a binding that names a missing file used to fail the try with no reason.

## What changes

A stub task that no Dag processor bound, queued for example before the first parse after an upgrade, now fails its try with the reason in its task log and as its state reason, and retries apply:

```
Task 'load' of Dag 'etl' has no task handler artifact, and its Dag file 'etl.py' is not an artifact that ExecutableCoordinator runs. Queue 'golang' routes it to a Lang-SDK coordinator, so it must be a @task.stub task the Dag processor bound to an artifact, or a task of a Dag defined in a Lang SDK. Check the import errors of 'etl.py', and that the scheduler has the same [sdk] configuration as the Dag processor.
```

For a coordinator author, one hook now starts an artifact for the probe and the task, another says which files a task may run, and a coordinator that is not subprocess based raises one error before its runtime starts:

```python
class MyCoordinator(SubprocessCoordinator):
    def _read_task_handler_candidate(self, path, *, rel_path): ...  # None: not one of my artifacts; error: it cannot run
    def _build_task_handler_command(self, *, path): ...  # was _build_parse_task_handler_command; the task uses it too


raise TaskHandlerArtifactError("...")  # from execute_task, before the runtime starts
```

- **Failing in the task runtime.** `supervise_task` catches `TaskHandlerArtifactError`, starts the task instance, writes the reason to the task log and the supervisor log, reports the try as up for retry or failed with the reason (redacted, cut to 500 characters) as its state reason, uploads the log and exits with 1. A task cleared while it was queued reports no state, and a task already running elsewhere raises as before. Task callbacks do not run, as for every coordinator task failure (#74063). A runtime that fails to start is not covered, as before.
- **Running exactly one file.** A task runs the file its workload references, in the bundle the reference names (or the task's own bundle at the version the run uses, as before). Without a reference it runs its own Dag file in its own bundle, which is how a task of a Dag defined in a Lang SDK runs. `task_handler_bundle_name` is no longer read at execution.
- **Checks before the runtime starts.** The file must be in the bundle, `_read_task_handler_candidate` must return a candidate without an error (so a stub task's Python file fails, and so does a Go bundle without the executable bit), `_build_task_handler_command` must build the command (the integrity check), and the schema version, when there is one, must be one the supervisor knows. Each failure is a `TaskHandlerArtifactError` that gives the reason and names the file and its Dag bundle (the unbound-stub reason names the task, its Dag file and its queue instead). A file the worker cannot open gives the error as its reason, and a schema version the worker's Task SDK does not know says so instead of the migrator's text. A coordinator without a hook fails its tasks naming the hooks it lacks.
- **The scan is deleted.** `_build_execute_task_command`, the Go and TypeScript `_Bundle.find`, the Java `_JarInfo` and `ResolvedBundle` are gone. The Java classpath uses the sorted `walk_files` (same JARs, same order). The TypeScript reader no longer requires `task_handlers` in the bundle metadata, and does not read it.
- **Java `main_class`** now also runs the probe, so a handler JAR without a manifest `Main-Class` is listed and probed when it is set. Without it the bound JAR's manifest decides, which ends the arbitrary pick between JARs that declare a `Main-Class` (#71134). With it every handler JAR in the bundle reports the same handlers, so keep one per bundle. The digest recorded for a JAR covers `main_class` when it is set (it is the manifest's digest when unset), so changing `main_class` makes the Dag processor probe the JARs again. A thin JAR takes its schema version from the first JAR with one, in sorted path order.
- **e2e.** The Lang-SDK compose modes skip `airflow dags reserialize`, which writes stub Dags without bindings and would fail a task queued before the Dag processor binds it. The Dag processor commits bindings with the Dag rows, and `trigger_dag` waits for the Dag.
- **Docs.** The language pages, the Language SDK guide, the bundle specs, the contributor guide for a new Language SDK, the READMEs, the Java and new SDK agent skills, the harness text and ADRs 0011 to 0013 say a worker runs the bound artifact and nothing else. The Java page lists the manifest attributes a Maven-built handler JAR needs (`Airflow-Cache-Digest`, `Main-Class`, `Airflow-Supervisor-Schema-Version`), with a digest that changes on every build; the Gradle plugin writes them. Upgrade the Dag processor, the scheduler and the workers together: a task queued without its artifact by an older scheduler fails with the reason, and retries apply.

<details>
<summary>Messages</summary>

These strings are kept stable for the later PRs of the stack, which assert on them. `{origin}` is `Task handler artifact` for a file a workload references, or `Dag file` for the task's own Dag file. Two log events go to the task log:

- `Running a Lang-SDK artifact`, with `origin`, `bundle_name`, `bundle_version` and `path`.
- `Cannot run the task's Lang-SDK artifact`, with `reason`. The supervisor log gets it too, as a warning with `ti_id` and `reason`.

Every final reason, as `TaskHandlerArtifactError` raises it:

- A stub task with no binding whose Dag file is not an artifact of the coordinator, filled in with the task, Dag, Dag file, queue and coordinator class name: `Task 'load' of Dag 'etl' has no task handler artifact, and its Dag file 'etl.py' is not an artifact that ExecutableCoordinator runs. Queue 'golang' routes it to a Lang-SDK coordinator, so it must be a @task.stub task the Dag processor bound to an artifact, or a task of a Dag defined in a Lang SDK. Check the import errors of 'etl.py', and that the scheduler has the same [sdk] configuration as the Dag processor.`
- A referenced file that is not in its bundle: `Task handler artifact 'bin/etl' is not a file in Dag bundle 'go-task-handlers' at version 'abc'.` The ` at version 'abc'` part is left out when the bundle has no version.
- A referenced file of another coordinator: `Task handler artifact 'bin/etl' in Dag bundle 'go-task-handlers' is not an artifact that ExecutableCoordinator runs. A newer parse may route this task to another coordinator.`
- A file that cannot run: `{origin} 'bin/etl' in Dag bundle 'go-task-handlers' cannot run: {reason}`. The reason is one of:
  - The error from a file or a parent directory the worker cannot open or search, or one that `_read_task_handler_candidate` raises, such as `[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/path/to/bin/etl'`.
  - The reason the coordinator gives for the file, such as `bin/etl is not executable. Use a Dag bundle that keeps the executable bit; object-store Dag bundles such as S3DagBundle drop it.`
  - The error of `_build_task_handler_command`, such as an integrity check that fails.
  - An unknown supervisor schema version: `uses supervisor schema version '1999-01-01', which this worker's Task SDK does not support`.
- A bundle that cannot be read: `{origin} 'bin/etl' cannot run: Dag bundle 'go-task-handlers' cannot be read: {reason}`. The reason is the error of the bundle, or `it resolved to /path/to/bundle, which does not exist.`
- A coordinator without the hooks: `MyCoordinator cannot run tasks: implement _read_task_handler_candidate and _build_task_handler_command.` It names only the hooks that are missing.

The Dag processor's probe is not covered: it reports an unknown supervisor schema version as before, with the migrator's text in the import error of the stub Dag.
